text:
Priya: quick triage — approx decoding + 4-bit PTQ on llama3-13b shows a consistent quality drop on our summarization bench. numbers below, tagging infra/ops. :eyes:

Tom: can you paste the exact run args and the quant config?

Priya: run command we used: `runtest --model=llama3-13b --quant=ptq-4bit --decode=approximate-spec --batch=1 --seed=42`

Aisha: results snapshot: mean ROUGE-L: baseline fp16 0.462 -> ptq-4bit approx 0.433 (-6.3%), latency median 90ms -> 62ms (good). Looks like quality hit scales with sequence length.

Jorge: interesting — throughput/latency win is nice but regression on long docs is worrying. Any difference between `approximate-spec` and `speculative`?

Priya: approx decode is our lighter-weight speculative variant (single-pass prefix prefetch, looser acceptance threshold). speculative is two-stage with verification. We tried both; approximation had larger drop.

Tom: can we repro with pure fp16 + approx decode to isolate quantization vs algorithm?

Aisha: yes — ran fp16 + approx: ROUGE-L 0.458 -> tiny drop vs fp16 baseline (-0.9%). So most regression seems quantization + approx interaction.

Eve: do we have per-token divergence trace? maybe early tokens fine then drift.

Priya: uploaded a short trace and divergence plot here: https://perf.redwood.internal/bench/1234 (look at seq>1024). Also attaching minimal logs: 
```
[run id=run-20260320-01] model=llama3-13b quant=ptq-4bit decode=approximate-spec
seq=128 ROUGE-L delta -1.1%
seq=512 ROUGE-L delta -3.2%
seq=2048 ROUGE-L delta -7.8%
```

Jorge: that pattern screams conditioning-stability issue — kv-cache precision loss causing sampling noise later. Worth checking KV quant scales.

Tom: ops question — is this happening on our dedicated pool only or hosted infra too?

Priya: repro on both dedicated and hosted when using the same quant artifact. Hosted has slight additional variance but same direction.

Aisha: hypothesis: the approx early-accept threshold uses logits margin; quant noise reduces margin and causes more early accepts -> lower tail quality. I can run ablation where we tighten accept threshold and/or force verification step.

Priya: please run two quick ablations: 1) ptq-4bit + approx with accept-threshold +0.8 (stricter), 2) ptq-4bit + approx but force fallback to full verification for tokens after 512. Compare ROUGE-L/latency.

ops-ci-bot: nightly-quality-check: run run-20260320-01 -> FAILURE (ROUGE-L drop > 4% relative to fp16 baseline). See job: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/789

Jorge: also try mixed-precision KV (store KV in fp16 even if weights are quantized) — that sometimes removes the drift.

Tom: we should also log random-seed variance; small sample sizes can amplify apparent regressions. How many eval samples?

Aisha: 200 examples per seq-bucket. variance is small (±0.3%) on baseline; the deltas here are well outside noise.

Priya: action items: Aisha run the two ablations + mixed-KV test; Tom/Infra check quant artifact for asymmetric clipping or per-channel scale instabilities; Jorge run a quick smoke on hosted region us-west2. We'll reconvene in ~2 hours.

Eve: flagging this for canary hold — don't push ptq-4bit approx to traffic until we have mitigations. :warning:

Aisha: starting ablation now, will drop logs in /tmp/approx-ablation-1795556666.tar.gz when done.

Tom: will inspect quantizer codepath (per-channel vs per-tensor) — if it's per-tensor for KV that could explain drift.

Priya: thanks all. if anyone hits something urgent ping me directly. :rocket:
